doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Why jazz is a challenge for listeners
summary: They discuss jazz's small market share and an attention-deficit culture that favors sound bites over complexity.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Jazz right now I guess sells about three percent of the —
Yeah, I guess three or less is what I heard recently.
In your mind is there a reason that jazz is let’s say more of a challenge for the listener?

Yeah. And I think our culture unfortunately as a large group is evolving more and more into a kind of attention deficit culture, so that people’s attention span is for a sound bite, a quick image on MTV, a repetitive hook composition, whatever the genre. But to get someone to sit down and really sink into say a ten minute composition that has a number of parts and complexities and improvisation, a small segment of the listening population willing to reach out and meet the music halfway that way. It seems like people are willing to reach out this much, not that much, as a group. It’s always a big treat when we play a concert or play in a club where people, even if they came in doubting what they were able to do, sometimes the positive contagion of a live event where some others are getting into the music will help other people reach out. But it’s disturbing when I think of the culture at large, how rather than progressing in terms of being able to embrace complexity, the culture as a whole seems to be going in the opposite direction.
Yeah. What’s the number one cause of that in your mind?

I guess in some ways if there’s a lot of material out there that sort of panders to the lowest common denominator, and there’s a certain inherent laziness in people, if they can quickly get some fast food they may not want to sit down and have a beautifully prepared seven course gourmet meal. They’ll just gobble and go on to the next.
As if we’re all so busy that we have to do that.
You know the media says that they only reflect the culture or what people want. And critics of the media say I don’t know, I think you’re causing it to happen.
Sure, it’s a very reciprocal kind of dance that goes on.
